title: The City of Gears
summary: The southern highlands of Brazil, 2773. Over an old mine Meister Hollweg founds Concórdia, a city that governs itself. The valley below fears it from the first day.

sides.name: The Guild
sides.about: Meister Hollweg's guild and its families, founding a city on the southern highlands.

sides.name: The Valley
sides.about: The colonists of the valley below: Captain Arruda's militia, the ranchers, the town and its priest.

objectives.text: Raise the Clocktower over the mine's old shaft: send your Winders to its site. Everything in the city runs from it.
objectives.phone: Raise the Clocktower: Winders to its site.

objectives.text: Build the Mainspring at its site beside the Escapement. It winds the Tension the Clock Aviary and its Swifts are made with.
Build the Cog Press at its site north of the tower: it brings the cogs that pay for soldiers at the Light Works.
Build the CLOCK AVIARY at its site: the machines' birds fly from it.
Make two Swifts at the Clock Aviary: {swifts} of 2. Pick the Aviary and press SWIFT.

Map the three ways up to the plateau: {mapped} of 3. Fly a Swift over the cart road (west), the pine path (north-west) and the ranch track (south). The land stays dark, and whoever walks on it unseen, until a Swift has flown over it.
objectives.phone: Map the three ways up: {mapped} of 3. Fly a Swift over each.

objectives.text: The valley's captain rides up the cart road in {clock:captain}.
The valley's captain waits on the cart road below the west ramp to talk. Walk Meister Hollweg down to him and keep him there a moment: the council's speaker goes with him.
The valley's men are on the plateau: drive them off. {raid_left} left.
The first quarter must stand: {houses} of {houses_n} houses.
Meister Hollweg must live. Hurt, he falls back to the tower.

The valley's people come up the road with torches. Your machines will strike no man of the valley: TURN THEM BACK (stand fighters round one, none of the militia by him, a moment) and PUT OUT the fires (any of your men by a burning building). Turned back: {turned_back}.
objectives.phone: Turn the torch-bearers back (fighters round one) and put out fires. Turned back: {turned_back}.

objectives.text: The valley's temper: {temper} of {temper_top}. Every fire raises it, a burnt house twice; at the top the militia rides at once.
The crates of 2767 lie in the mine's deepest gallery (north-east, behind the spoil heaps). Bring Meister Hollweg there and keep him there a while: only he knows the seal.
The valley's militia attacks at dawn, up all three ways. Hold the city until the attack breaks: {attack_left} of the attackers left.
objectives.phone: Hold the city until the attack breaks: {attack_left} left.

objectives.text: Burn the city's first quarter before it takes root: {houses} houses stand. Torches set them alight; muskets do the rest.
Or bring down the Clocktower, or Meister Hollweg himself.

deny.why: Hollweg is drawing the Heavy Works again from memory: not yet.

k_open1.text: He named it for concord. The valley named it otherwise.

k_open2.text: Two years after he left my Crown, Hollweg bought a dead mine at the bottom of the world, and built a city on it that answered to nobody.

h_open1.text: A city that governs itself. A council of masters, every voice a wheel, and the wheels in time. That was the plan.

h_open2.text: Rome had said those very words were a sin. I said them louder.

h_open_v.text: A ship from Lisbon brought us a man I never thought I would need: Etienne Varenne, the Assembly's orator, whom the King had spared and sent away.

h_open_m.text: A ship from Lisbon brought us one of the Assembly's men, Citizen Morel. Varenne was dead. Morel had not forgiven anyone for it.

h_1.text: The tower first. Over the old shaft, where the ground is sound. Everything else turns round it.

u_tip1.text: The tower's site is marked by the shaft, Meister. Send the Winders; four hands raise it quickly.

u_dark.text: And look how little we know of this place. Everything off the plateau is dark to us: anyone could walk up those roads and we would not see him.

h_tower.text: The tower stands. Now the spring, then the birds. I want this country mapped from the air, every road, before the first winter.

u_field.text: The tower's gears are turning, Meister. Keep the soldiers on the gear rings round our buildings: there they stay wound. Off the gears they run down in a minute or so.

u_spring.text: The Aviary runs on Tension, Meister, and Tension comes from the Mainspring. Its site is by the Escapement.

u_presses.text: While the Aviary rises: the city has cogs for now, not for ever. The press north of the tower brings more, and the Light Works turns them into soldiers.

u_aviary.text: The spring is wound. Now the Aviary: its site is east of the tower. A Winder or two will raise it.

u_swifts.text: The Aviary is up. Pick it and make Swifts. Little brass birds: they fight only other birds, but they see a long way.

h_map.text: Fly them down the three ways: the cart road west, the pine path north-west, the ranch track south. What a bird has seen, the guild knows.

h_mapped_all.text: There. The whole country under one eye. From above, every road is only a gear's tooth.

v_1.text: A city without a lord, Meister. I have heard this sermon before. I preached it, in Virginia and in Paris.

h_v1.text: Yours was made of men, Varenne. Mine is made of wheels. Wheels keep time.

v_2.text: Paris burned keeping time. I watched it from a boat.

m_1.text: No lord and no bishop. Good. Then let the valley learn it too, Meister, and quickly.

h_m1.text: The valley can learn what it likes. We did not come here to teach.

h_crates_seen.text: Somewhere under us lie the two crates I sent from Nuremberg. They had lain on a quay in the jungle once, I learned later.

h_memory.text: No Heavy Works yet. I build it from memory, and memory is slow. The drawings are in Nuremberg, or in the Crown's hands.

u_late.text: Meister, the valley has seen our tents and our machines for days, and no tower up. They will not wait for us to be ready.

u_captain.text: A rider from the valley, Meister. Their captain, coming up the cart road.

a_wait.text: I am Bento Arruda, captain of the valley's militia. I will talk with the master of this place. Here, on the road. Not up there among those things.

u_parley.text: He wants to talk, Meister. Walk down to him: the council's speaker will go with you. We will keep the machines back.

a_parley1.text: My people say you raise the devil's own works up here. Clocks that walk. They say it was such things that ended the old world.

h_parley.text: They are tools, Captain. I have ordered them never to raise a hand against a man of your valley. Not one.

v_parley.text: Captain, I have stood where you stand, at the head of frightened men. Go home. Nobody here wants your land.

m_parley.text: Your priests have told you to fear us. Ask yourself who profits by your fear, Captain.

a_parley2.text: I will take your word down the hill. I cannot promise they will believe it.

n_parley.text: The captain rides home without a blow struck.

a_nobody.text: Nobody comes down to talk. So be it.

u_raid.text: Riders on the cart road, Meister, and muskets! The valley does not mean to talk.

u_raid_dark.text: I hear horses on the dark roads, Meister, and I cannot see them. The Swifts!

h_raid_over.text: They have gone back down. Let them. Mend what they broke.

u_dusk.text: The sun is going down over the valley, Meister. There are lights on the road. Many lights.

n_fear.text: Night. The people of the valley come up the cart road with torches and scythes. No soldiers: farmers, drovers, their wives.

h_fear.text: Nobody strikes them. Do you hear me? Not one blow. I saw Rome burn. It will not start again here, and not by my machines.

u_fear.text: Then we stand in their way, Meister. Put fighters round a man with a torch and he will think better of it. Shields up: they throw stones.

u_fire.text: A house is burning! Anyone, to the fire: a man of ours beside it puts it out.

n_crowd3.text: The last of them, and the angriest.

m_fear.text: Let the machines teach them, Meister. One lesson tonight saves a hundred later.

h_m_fear.text: No, Citizen. I have seen the end of that lesson.

v_fear.text: Hold, Meister. Hold. A crowd that is not struck goes home in the end. A crowd that is struck never does.

u_temper.text: The fires are seen from the valley, Meister. Every one makes them angrier.

n_anselmo.text: A priest comes up the road alone, in a black cassock, with a lantern.

p_1.text: Enough! Is this how a Christian keeps the Sabbath, with a torch in his hand on a stranger's hill?

p_2.text: Home, all of you. If these men are wrong, God and the Church will judge them, not your torches.

n_home.text: The people of the valley lower their torches and go down the road behind their priest.

h_anselmo.text: He did with one word what all my shields could not do. I wrote that down. I did not understand it until much later.

n_boil.text: The valley sees the plateau burning. The bells ring in the town, and the militia saddles at once.

h_boil.text: They are coming with muskets now. Into the tower's field, all of you. We hold.

n_house_lost.text: A house of the first quarter has burned down.

n_dawn.text: Dawn over the highlands, grey and cold. The valley is quiet. Too quiet.

h_crates1.text: The crates. Before anything else today, I want to see the crates. Ulrich, the lantern.

u_crates.text: The deepest gallery is behind the spoil heaps, Meister, north-east. The seal will know your hand.

n_opened.text: The crates of 2767 are opened. Inside, the guild's best work of Nuremberg, packed in straw, perfect.

h_opened.text: Two soldiers of a pattern I do not remember drawing. A Winder. And plates, so many plates. My best work. It must have been.

u_plates.text: The plates are lying across the gallery floor, Meister. I did not see anyone lay them.

h_plates.text: They slid out of the straw. Leave them. They wind whatever stands on them: a gift.

h_jakob.text: Jakob would have counted the teeth on those plates. Jakob was in Fürth.

u_attack.text: Meister! The militia, up all three roads at once! Riders on the ranch track!

a_attack.text: For the valley, and for God! Burn the tower!

a_attack_p.text: I gave them your word, clockmaker. The night gave them theirs. Forgive me.

h_attack.text: These are soldiers. Defend the city. Shields to the front, the Winders behind.

n_path.text: More of them out of the pines, by the north-west path.

a_break.text: Back! Back down the hill! Enough have died for one morning.

n_break.text: The militia breaks and goes down the hill. The city stands.

h_hurt.text: I am hit. Keep them off the tower, never mind me.

n_tower_lost.text: The Clocktower has fallen. Without it the city is a camp of tents again.

n_quarter_lost.text: Every house of the first quarter is ash. The families sleep in the tents, and some take the road to the coast.

a_v1.text: There it is, on our hill: the thing the old world died of. Burn their houses before they take root, or bring the tower down.

a_v_tip.text: The Barracks in the town and the Horse Breeder at the ranches are ours. The people will go up the road tonight whatever we do.

h_end1.text: By the first winter the city had a wall of timber, a council and a name. I sat at the head of the council table and called it concord.

h_end_parley.text: The valley's captain had taken my word down the hill. That word was the best thing I built that year.

h_end_fought.text: The valley never forgave us that dawn. Its people crossed themselves when our birds flew over.

h_end_v.text: Varenne spoke for the city's people in the council. He was the only one of us who was afraid of it. I thought it was the habit of exile.

h_end_m.text: Morel spoke for the city's people in the council, and wanted the valley taught. I would not have it. That much I had learned in Rome.

h_end2.text: I had learned to hold my machines back from the valley. I had not learned to hold them back from themselves.

k_end1.text: The plates in that gallery were not his best work. They were the Perpetual's. He had sent them ahead himself, six years before.

k_end_people.text: He had left the pattern in Nuremberg. He had already sent it ahead.

k_end2.text: A priest of the valley stopped a crowd that night with two sentences. Hollweg wrote it down. It took him twenty years to read it.

k_end_v.text: The valley burned the city's first houses on its first night. That is not how it went. It stood, and grew.

a_end_v.text: We burned it before it took root. The bishop wrote to thank us. I did not sleep well, all the same.

new_cuckoo_house.text: NEW: THE CLOCK AVIARY. A tall clock with little doors: the machines' birds fly from it. It needs a working Escapement, and runs on Tension: a Mainspring in its gear field.

new_cuckoo.text: NEW: THE SWIFT. A fast brass bird made at the Clock Aviary. It fights only other flyers, but it sees far: here the land off the plateau stays dark until a Swift has flown over it.

mine.caption: The southern highlands, 2773. The old mine where the guild raises its tower.

fear.caption: The valley's fear: the road at night.

exile.caption: A ship from Lisbon, and a man the King had spared.

rome.caption: Rome, the present. The King listens; the clockmaker tells it.

text: The southern highlands of Brazil, 2773. Meister Hollweg's guild has bought an old mine and means to build a city over it: Concórdia, governed by its own council.
Raise the Clocktower, build the CLOCK AVIARY and fly its Swifts over the three ways up: off the plateau the land is dark until a bird has seen it.
The valley below fears the machines. Its people will come at night: turn them back without a blow. Then open the crates of 2767, and hold the city at dawn.
The southern highlands, 2773. You lead the valley's militia under Captain Arruda. Strangers with walking machines have taken the old mine on the hill.
Burn their first houses, bring down their tower, or bring down their master, before the city takes root.

guild.title: Concórdia
guild.text: The city stands. {houses} of {houses_n} houses of the first quarter stand; {turned_back} of the valley's people were turned back without a blow.

text_if.text: The valley's captain parleyed with Hollweg on the road.
The valley fought the city from its first day.
The crates of 2767 were opened in the mine.

valley.title: Burned before it took root
valley.text: The valley's militia drove the guild's city off the hill.
